programMetadata.objective: Max Explosive Power, Vascularity, and Pelvic Stamina
programMetadata.equipmentAccess: Full Gym: Barbell, Trap Bar, Cables, Dumbbells, Kettlebells, Landmine, Treadmill
programMetadata.keyCoachingTheme: Explosive Power, V-Taper Hypertrophy, Hip Endurance, Mobility, Vascularity
programMetadata.brandHierarchy: PHANTOM H&P is the parent performance company. LIFT GHOST is the training app powered by Phantom H&P.

auxiliaryBlocks.blockName: AM IGNITION - Daily Morning Wake-Up Starter
auxiliaryBlocks.coachCommand: Prime. Mobilize. Do not create fatigue before the main training day.

exercises.setup: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart. Keep knees soft, core lightly braced, and weight over the balls of the feet.
exercises.howTo: Make a small bounce using mostly the ankles, not a deep knee bend. Land quietly on the balls of the feet and rebound right away. Keep the torso upright and the contacts quick and low. Stop if the calves/Achilles feel sharp pain rather than normal warm-up tension.

exercises.setup: Use a very light resistance band and take a wide overhand grip. Stand tall with arms straight, ribs down, and shoulders relaxed.
exercises.howTo: Start with the band in front of the thighs. Move the straight arms up and overhead, then gently behind the body. Only travel as far as the shoulders move comfortably without arching the low back. Reverse the same path to return to the front.

exercises.setup: Take a wide stance with toes slightly turned out. Keep both feet planted and chest tall before shifting to one side.
exercises.howTo: Shift the hips toward one leg while bending that knee. Keep the opposite leg long; let its toes turn up if needed for comfort. Descend only as far as you can keep balance and control. Drive through the bent leg to return to center, then repeat on the other side.

exercises.setup: Take a long split stance with the front foot flat. Use a rack or support for balance if needed during the warm-up.
exercises.howTo: Let the front knee travel forward over the toes while the heel stays down. Lower the back knee toward the floor and keep the torso controlled. Reach a comfortable deep position without forcing the ankle, knee, or hip. Push through the front foot to rise, complete the reps, then switch sides.

exercises.setup: Choose the prescribed hip-opening position and enter it slowly. Use padding or support as needed so you can relax instead of fighting for balance.
exercises.howTo: Ease into the stretch until you feel firm but comfortable tension. Breathe slowly and keep the spine controlled instead of bouncing. Hold the position for the prescribed time. Come out gradually, then change sides or move to the next stretch.

days.focus: Box Squat, Trap Bar Deadlift, Hip Thrust, Kettlebell Swing, Incline Walk
days.coachCommand: Own the brace. Move heavy weight with clean power. Keep every rep controlled enough to repeat.

exercises.setup: Place a stable box inside the rack at the programmed squat depth. Set the safety arms correctly and position the bar across the upper back. Unrack, take a controlled step back, and set the feet in your normal squat stance.
exercises.howTo: Take a breath and brace the trunk before descending. Sit the hips back and bend the knees while keeping the whole foot planted. Touch the box under control - do not crash, rock, or fully relax onto it. Drive through the floor to stand tall, reset your breath/bracing, and repeat.

exercises.setup: Load the trap bar evenly and stand centered inside it with feet about hip-width. Hinge down, grip both handles evenly, flatten the back, and brace before lifting.
exercises.howTo: Push the floor away while extending the knees and hips together. Keep the bar level and let the arms stay long; do not curl or shrug the handles up. Finish tall with hips and knees straight without leaning backward. Hinge the hips back, bend the knees, and lower the bar under control to the floor.

exercises.setup: Place the upper back against a stable bench and use a pad on the bar. Center the bar over the hip crease and plant the feet about shoulder-width.
exercises.howTo: Brace the ribs down and drive through the heels to lift the hips. At the top, finish with the torso roughly level and shins close to vertical. Squeeze the glutes for the programmed 2 seconds without over-arching the low back. Lower the hips under control and repeat without letting the bar roll.

exercises.setup: Place the kettlebell slightly in front of you with feet about shoulder-width. Hinge at the hips, grip the handle with both hands, and keep the back long and braced.
exercises.howTo: Hike the kettlebell back between the thighs like a football snap. Drive the hips forward hard and stand tall; let the bell float from the hip power. Keep the arms relaxed and avoid turning the swing into a front raise. Guide the bell back between the thighs, reload the hinge, and repeat.

exercises.setup: Choose a treadmill speed and incline you can sustain without holding the rails. Start easy, then increase the incline/speed gradually until you reach a steady Zone 2 effort.
exercises.howTo: Walk tall with a natural stride and relaxed arm swing. Keep breathing controlled; you should be working steadily, not sprinting. Adjust speed or incline if the effort drifts too high or too low. Continue for the full 20 minutes, then reduce the incline/speed gradually to cool down.

days.focus: Incline Press, Push Press, Rows, Dips, Lateral Raise/Curl Superset
days.coachCommand: Press with intent, row with control, and keep the finisher strict. Quality reps drive the V-taper.

exercises.setup: Set the bench to a moderate incline and position it evenly under the rack. Place the eyes just behind the bar, plant the feet, and pull the shoulder blades back/down. Take a secure grip and unrack without losing upper-back tension.
exercises.howTo: Lower the bar under control toward the upper chest. Keep forearms close to vertical and wrists stacked over the elbows. Touch lightly without bouncing, then press the bar up and slightly back toward the rack line. Finish each rep with the shoulders still packed and the feet planted.

exercises.setup: Rack the bar across the front shoulders with hands just outside shoulder-width. Stand about hip-width, brace the trunk, and keep the elbows in a position that supports the bar.
exercises.howTo: Dip straight down a few inches by bending the knees and hips together. Drive the floor away explosively and transfer the leg power into the bar. As the bar rises, press it overhead until the arms are extended and body is stacked. Lower the bar under control to the shoulders, reset, and repeat.

exercises.setup: Use a stable bench or strong split stance for support. Brace the torso so the spine stays long and square to the floor. Let the working arm hang long with the dumbbell under the shoulder.
exercises.howTo: Pull the elbow back toward the hip/ribcage instead of straight up toward the shoulder. Keep the torso mostly still - avoid twisting to create momentum. Squeeze the back briefly at the top. Lower the dumbbell until the arm is long again while keeping the shoulder controlled.

exercises.setup: Set the cable attachment and load, sit tall, and brace the feet securely. Take the wide grip with arms long and torso upright before starting.
exercises.howTo: Drive the elbows back with intent while keeping the chest tall. Pull the handle toward the upper abdomen/lower chest according to the attachment path. Squeeze the upper back without leaning far behind vertical. Return the arms forward under control and keep tension instead of letting the stack slam.

exercises.setup: Use stable parallel bars and start supported with elbows extended. Set the shoulders down away from the ears and keep the torso controlled.
exercises.howTo: Bend the elbows and lower the body smoothly. Descend only to a comfortable shoulder depth while keeping the bars under control. Press the bars down to return to the top without bouncing out of the bottom. End the set when you can no longer maintain the same depth and shoulder position.

exercises.setup: Set the cable at a low position and use a load that allows the full rep range without swinging. Stand tall with the working shoulder controlled and the cable positioned for a smooth lateral path.
exercises.howTo: Keep a soft elbow and raise the arm out to about shoulder height without shrugging. Pause briefly with the shoulder controlled. Lower the cable slowly to the start position. Complete the prescribed reps, then transition to the paired curl.

exercises.setup: Place the dumbbells nearby for a quick transition from the cable lateral raise. Choose a load that allows the full rep range without rocking the torso.
exercises.howTo: Stand tall and keep the elbows close to the sides. Curl the dumbbells without swinging or leaning backward. Squeeze at the top, then lower fully under control. Rest after both exercises in the superset are complete.

days.focus: Depth Jump, Single-Leg Jump, Slam Ball Chain, Bodyweight Circuit, Carries/Planks
days.coachCommand: Explosive quality first. Reset between efforts. Stop the set when landing, sequence, or posture breaks down.

exercises.setup: Use a low, stable drop platform and a separate landing box at an appropriate height. Clear the landing area and make sure the box cannot slide.
exercises.howTo: Step off the platform - do not jump upward from it. Land on both feet softly and absorb the drop with the hips and knees. Transition quickly into a powerful two-foot jump onto the box. Land quietly on the box with knees tracking over the toes, stand stable, then step down and reset.

exercises.displayName: Seated Single-Leg Stand Up to Jump
exercises.sourceName: Seated Single-Leg Stand Up to Jump
exercises.setup: Sit near the front of a stable bench/box with one foot firmly planted. Keep the other foot off the floor and choose a seat height that allows a controlled single-leg stand.
exercises.howTo: Lean the torso slightly forward while keeping the planted foot flat. Drive through the planted leg to stand as explosively as possible. Transition into the programmed jump only after you have control of the takeoff. Land softly, regain balance, sit/reset fully, complete the reps, then switch sides.

exercises.setup: Use the exact slam-ball weight and stage order prescribed by the coach. Clear enough floor space for every direction in the complex and confirm the ball will not rebound dangerously.
exercises.howTo: Start each stage from the coach-defined position and keep the ball close during transitions. Brace before each explosive throw/slam and use the whole body rather than only the arms. Complete the stages in the programmed order with deliberate footwork and control. If you lose the sequence, spacing, or ball path, stop and reset instead of improvising the complex.
exercises.notes: Preserve as one source record until Lift Ghost/user resolves it to a saved production complex or exact child stages.

exercises.setup: Use a stable dip station and begin each round from a controlled support position. Set the shoulders down away from the ears before the first rep.
exercises.howTo: Lower under control to a comfortable depth. Press back to the top without bouncing out of the bottom. Maintain the same depth and shoulder position throughout. Transition safely to the next circuit station.

exercises.setup: Use a secure pull-up bar and take the prescribed wide grip. Begin from an active hang with the trunk controlled.
exercises.howTo: Pull the chest toward the bar without excessive swinging. Keep the body controlled through the top position. Lower under control until the arms are long again. Transition safely to the next circuit station.

exercises.setup: Use clear, non-slip floor space and set a rigid plank position. Place the hands in a stable push-up position before beginning.
exercises.howTo: Lower smoothly while keeping the body rigid. Press explosively enough for the hands to leave the floor. Land with soft elbows and immediately regain control. Stop the movement when technique breaks down.

exercises.setup: Choose loads you can hold without leaning and clear a straight walking lane. Stand tall with the weights close to the sides before moving.
exercises.howTo: Brace the trunk and walk with short controlled steps. Keep the shoulders level and avoid leaning toward either weight. Maintain steady breathing throughout the carry. Stop or reset if posture breaks down.
exercises.notes: Source provides one shared 45s CORE-HOLDS target; it is not assigned separately to this movement.

exercises.displayName: Side Planks w/ Active Kegel Holds
exercises.sourceName: Side Planks w/ Active Kegel Holds
exercises.setup: Use a non-slip mat and stack the elbow under the shoulder. Set the body in a straight side-plank position and use a gentle pelvic-floor contraction rather than a maximal strain.
exercises.howTo: Lift the hips so the head, ribs, pelvis, and legs form one line. Gently contract the pelvic floor while continuing to breathe normally. Maintain the hold without bearing down or losing trunk position. Release the contraction if breath-holding or form breakdown occurs.
exercises.notes: Canonical production identity is Side Plank. Active Kegel Hold remains Phantom coaching wording; source shared 45s target is not copied to this child.

days.focus: Landmine Jerk, Explosive Split Squat, Speed Bench, Single-Arm Incline DB Bench, Conditioning
days.coachCommand: Move fast under control. Bar speed and clean mechanics matter more than load chasing.

exercises.setup: Secure the bar in a landmine attachment and load the sleeve evenly. Hold the sleeve at shoulder height on the working side and stand in a stable athletic stance.
exercises.howTo: Brace, then make a short controlled dip through the knees and hips. Drive the legs hard and send the bar up and forward using the lower-body impulse. Finish stable with the working arm extended in line with the landmine path. Lower the sleeve back to the shoulder under control, reset the stance, and repeat.
exercises.notes: Do not substitute Landmine Push Press.

exercises.setup: Set a stable split stance with enough front-to- back distance to descend comfortably. Brace the trunk and use the prescribed external load/position consistently on both sides.
exercises.howTo: Lower under control by bending both knees while keeping the front foot planted. Drive through the front foot as explosively as possible. Maintain hip, knee, and foot alignment throughout the rep. Regain full balance and reset the stance before beginning the next repetition.
exercises.notes: Do not assume Split Squat Jump.

exercises.setup: Set up exactly like a normal bench press with feet planted and shoulder blades locked to the bench. Use the programmed 50-60% 1RM load and secure collars on the bar.
exercises.howTo: Lower the bar under control to the same touch point each rep. Keep the upper back tight and avoid bouncing the bar off the chest. Press the bar as fast as possible while maintaining the same safe bar path. Re-rack carefully after the set; speed should never replace control.

exercises.setup: Set the bench to a moderate incline and sit with one dumbbell at the working shoulder. Plant the feet and brace the torso so the body does not rotate toward the weight.
exercises.howTo: Lower the dumbbell under control beside the upper chest/ shoulder. Keep the wrist stacked and shoulder packed. Press explosively while keeping the torso square to the bench. Control the return, finish the reps on one side, then switch arms.

exercises.setup: Set up the rope and clear enough floor space to turn it safely. Use a rope length that allows smooth turns without excessive shoulder motion.
exercises.howTo: Stay tall and use small ankle-driven jumps. Keep the rope turns smooth and the elbows relatively close to the body. Maintain a sustainable rhythm within the 15-minute conditioning block. Transition according to the programmed jump-rope/sprint sequence.
exercises.notes: Parent conditioning block total is 15 min; child work duration, transition, recovery, and rounds are unresolved.

exercises.setup: Complete an appropriate sprint warm-up before high-speed running. Use a clear running lane or appropriate treadmill setup.
exercises.howTo: Accelerate progressively rather than reaching top speed instantly. Run with controlled mechanics and strong posture. Allow the programmed recovery between sprint efforts. Transition according to the programmed jump-rope/sprint sequence.
exercises.notes: Parent conditioning block total is 15 min; sprint work/recovery pattern is unresolved.

exercises.setup: Choose a treadmill incline/speed that is challenging but sustainable. Transition into the walk after the first 15- minute conditioning block rather than stopping abruptly.
exercises.howTo: Walk upright with a natural stride. Avoid hanging on the rails. Adjust speed or incline to maintain a steady effort. Continue for the full 15 minutes.

days.focus: Rear Delt Face Pulls, Light Walk, Long Tissue Stretching, Hydration Flush
days.coachCommand: Restore readiness. Keep recovery work easy enough that you finish fresher than you started.

exercises.setup: Attach a rope to a cable around upper-chest to face height. Use a light recovery-focused load and stand far enough back to keep tension on the cable.
exercises.howTo: Start tall with the arms extended and ribs controlled. Pull the rope toward the face while separating the hands and guiding the elbows out. Squeeze the rear shoulders/upper back without shrugging. Return slowly to the start and keep the movement easy enough to support recovery.
exercises.notes: Source does not uniquely select between production Cable Face Pull and Face Pulls.

exercises.setup: Choose an easy walking route or treadmill setting. Use a pace that feels restorative rather than demanding.
exercises.howTo: Keep the walk conversational and easy. Use relaxed posture and natural arm swing. The goal is circulation, not extra conditioning fatigue. Finish feeling fresher rather than depleted.
exercises.notes: Source permits route or treadmill; duration or distance is unresolved.

exercises.setup: Choose a calm area and use padding/support for stretches when needed. Enter each stretch slowly and stay within a comfortable range.
exercises.howTo: Move gradually into a comfortable stretch and hold without bouncing. Breathe normally and relax into the position. Avoid forcing painful end ranges. Come out slowly before changing positions.
exercises.notes: Preserve this generic recovery sequence for in-app/user resolution into named stretches or a verified saved recovery sequence.
